words.def: more than enough; in large amounts
words.ex: Berries are abundant in the woods in late summer.

words.def: to pay someone back for money they spent
words.ex: Mom will reimburse you for the snacks you bought for the class party.

words.def: to think something is bigger, better or easier than it really is
words.ex: I tend to overestimate how many pancakes I can eat.

words.def: with close, steady attention
words.ex: The cat watched the mouse hole intently.

words.def: to send out heat or light in all directions
words.ex: The wood stove will radiate warmth through the cabin.

words.def: the middle number in a list ordered from least to greatest
words.ex: In the list 2, 5 and 9, the median is 5.

words.def: to annoy or bother someone in a small but nagging way
words.ex: It will irk the coach if we show up late again.

words.def: to stop someone from doing what they planned
words.ex: A locked gate was enough to thwart the raccoons.

words.def: so clearly true that no one can argue
words.ex: The photo was indisputable proof that the dog had eaten the cake.

words.def: done in a careful, step-by-step way
words.ex: The methodical detective checked every room twice.

words.def: upset and worried because something bad happened
words.ex: We were dismayed to see rain on the day of the picnic.

words.def: to wake someone up or stir them to action
words.ex: The trumpet will rouse the campers at dawn.

words.def: to slowly wear away, usually by rust or chemicals
words.ex: Salt water can corrode metal boats.

words.def: coming after something else
words.ex: The first chapter was slow, but subsequent chapters were exciting.

words.def: the buying and selling of goods
words.ex: The river was busy with commerce between towns.

words.def: showing deep respect, especially for God or holy things
words.ex: The children were reverent and quiet during the prayer.

words.def: a note that tells where a fact or quote came from
words.ex: Add a citation for each book you used in your report.

words.def: extremely happy and excited
words.ex: I was ecstatic when I won the art contest.

words.def: embarrassed because of a silly mistake
words.ex: He gave a sheepish grin when he realized he had worn mismatched shoes.

words.def: a funny five-line poem with a bouncy rhythm
words.ex: My limerick was about a cat who wore a hat.

words.def: a short summary of the plot of a story
words.ex: The back cover gives a synopsis of the novel.

words.def: likely to spoil or go bad quickly
words.ex: Milk and fresh fish are perishable, so keep them in the refrigerator.

words.def: a story that tells what happened before an earlier story
words.ex: The prequel shows the old wizard as a young boy.

words.def: to form solid crystals
words.ex: When the sugar water cools, the sugar will crystallize on the string.

words.def: to walk slowly in an easy way, with no hurry
words.ex: The cows amble back to the barn at sunset.

words.def: to talk together to share ideas before deciding something
words.ex: The referees will confer before they make a ruling.

words.def: a newspaper article that gives the paper's own opinion
words.ex: The editorial argued that the town needs a new library.

words.def: calm, quiet and peaceful
words.ex: The lake was tranquil early in the morning.

words.def: having to do with how living things relate to each other and to their surroundings
words.ex: Cutting down the forest caused ecological damage to the river.

words.def: all the people who will live in the future
words.ex: We planted the oak trees for posterity.

words.def: able to be noticed or sensed, even if only a little
words.ex: There was a barely perceptible change in the color of the leaves.

words.def: a group of people chosen to study or take care of a special task
words.ex: The city formed a commission to plan the new park.

words.def: to include something as part of a whole
words.ex: We will incorporate your ideas into the plan.

words.def: dull because it never changes
words.ex: The monotonous hum of the fan put me to sleep.

words.def: to say something again in your own words
words.ex: Can you paraphrase what the teacher just said?

words.def: the shape and features of the land's surface
words.ex: The map shows the topography of the hills and valleys.

words.def: the rules or standards used to judge something
words.ex: The judges explained the criteria for the art contest.

words.def: a wall of earth built along a river to stop flooding
words.ex: The levee kept the river from spilling into the town.

words.def: belief in more than one god
words.ex: Many ancient peoples practiced polytheism.

words.def: kind and wanting to help others
words.ex: The benevolent king fed the hungry villagers.

words.def: to give someone the right to have or do something
words.ex: Your ticket will entitle you to one free drink.

words.def: fair, not favoring one side over another
words.ex: The judge must give an unbiased decision.

words.def: the number in front of a letter in math, which multiplies it
words.ex: In 7x, the coefficient is 7.

words.def: having all sides the same length
words.ex: Each side of the equilateral triangle measured five centimeters.

words.def: the order in which events happened
words.ex: We made a chronology of the events leading to the war.

words.def: a small raised number that tells how many times to multiply a number by itself
words.ex: In 2 to the third power, the exponent is 3.

words.def: the hunting and eating of one animal by another
words.ex: Rabbits have many young because so many are lost to predation.

words.def: a painting made on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling
words.ex: The fresco on the chapel ceiling showed angels and clouds.

words.def: to be very angry inside without showing it much
words.ex: He began to seethe when his sister took the last cookie.

words.def: to be full of living things moving around
words.ex: Tide pools teem with crabs and snails.

words.def: a close relationship between two different living things that helps them both
words.ex: The clownfish and the sea anemone live in symbiosis.

words.def: an ancient writing system of wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay
words.ex: Students in Sumer learned to write cuneiform on clay tablets.

words.def: a reason given against someone else's point
words.ex: She answered every counterargument with facts.

words.def: a tall, stepped temple tower built in ancient Mesopotamia
words.ex: The ziggurat rose high above the city's mud-brick homes.

words.def: how easily a substance can dissolve in a liquid
words.ex: Sugar has a high solubility in warm water.

words.def: a number that is much higher or lower than the rest of a set of data
words.ex: In the list 3, 4, 5 and 40, the number 40 is an outlier.

words.def: a bar graph that shows how many data values fall in each range
words.ex: The histogram showed most students sleep eight to nine hours.

words.def: the way plants give off water vapor through their leaves
words.ex: Transpiration pulls water up from the roots to the leaves.

words.def: a solid shape whose faces are all flat polygons
words.ex: A cube is a polyhedron with six square faces.

words.def: to confuse someone completely
words.ex: The tricky riddle seemed to befuddle everyone at the table.

words.def: to add notes to a text to explain it or mark ideas
words.ex: Please annotate the poem by circling words you don't know.

words.def: belief in only one God
words.ex: The religion was based on monotheism.
